Teletext will be removed from the project requirements; design priorities should focus on channel selection, volume, and power, and include a single settings button that opens audio/display options.
The remote will be used only for television control with no extra internet features; the scope is television-only and not for DVD/internet devices.
The target user group will be teenagers and young professionals in the 19-35 range.
The location feature will use RF signals to locate the remote, with a finder button and a buzzer or vibration to indicate location, and the location signal will be RF rather than IR.

The product packaging will be a two-part package with the remote and base sold separately; remotes will be general-purpose rather than VCR-specific; no VCR capabilities; focus on DVD-type functionality.

The button design will include a power button and numbers; the button count may be reduced by using a scrolling/joystick-like control; there will be four buttons for volume and channel control; the placement of the base mounting options will be deferred; a function-switch button will assign the circle disc to TV, DVD, or VCR mode to switch channels, volume, or menu accordingly.
The hold-one-to-power idea would be hard to implement.
Users may be confused about powering the device if there is no separate power button.
Users find it a big waste of time to learn how to use the remote, indicating a significant learning curve.
